correctness.rationale: At each terminal leaf, modalities reduce to constants 1 and 0 and the unary Gödel term algebra closes on precisely {0,1,x,not x,not-not x,x∨not x}; each function on (0,1] is constant 0, constant 1 or monotone identity and the value at zero is separately represented. For all finite leaf valuations, preserving a zero leaf if present plus smallest and largest positive p-values preserves extrema of all six functions. Every rooted Box/Diamond subformula therefore has its original value; structural induction including arbitrarily nested modal formulas and keeping the root p-value fixed gives all-formula equality simultaneously. Duplicate-leaf extension gives L_m=L3 for m>=3 including leaf-world validity; Box/Diamond agree on S1 and not S2; formula ¬Box p→(Diamond p→Box(p∨¬p)) is valid on S2 and fails at leaves 0,1/4,3/4 on S3. Independently checked the six function closure, 23,430 rational-grid terminal extrema cases, and both separators. Finite checks are not infinite or real-valued proofs; symbolic order-type reasoning and induction establish generality.

value.rationale: The underlying question is how many terminal successors an arbitrary one-variable crisp Gödel-modal root requires to preserve every observable formula value. The sharp formula-independent threshold three, plus the complete and strict one-variable frame-validity hierarchy, is a motivated structural expressivity classification rather than a small accidental count or rephrasing of decidability. Explicit separator formulas locate the irreducible branching information. The result has a natural use as a small-model/observational-equivalence fact precisely for the restricted one-variable star class.
residual_risks: Restricted to one variable, crisp nonreflexive depth-one stars; no multivariable or general Kripke-frame claim.
